newsitem.title: FINLAND: MAJORITY OF FINNISH MPS STAY SILENT ON EMU -POLL.
newsitem.headline: MAJORITY OF FINNISH MPS STAY SILENT ON EMU -POLL.

text.p: Four of five members of the Finnish parliament declined to state their opinion on whether Finland should join European economic and monetary union, a pro-EU lobby, said in a statement at the weekend.

All 200 MPs were asked to respond in writing to questions relating to EMU. Of the minority who gave their opinion on Finnish membership of EMU, 66 percent were largely in favour although many attached conditions to their support.
Nine MPs of pro-EMU Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's Social Democratic Party, the biggest in parliament and government, gave answers with eight cautiously for EMU and one firmly against.
All seven respondents from the Conservative Party led by pro-EMU Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto came out in favour of Finnish participation in the single currency.
Four MPs of the rainbow coalition's other left-wing party, the Leftist Alliance, took part in the survey with three in favour if certain conditions were met, and one solidly against.
Parliament is scheduled to vote about one year from now for or against Finnish membership of EMU.

Interpreting the findings of the survey made by polling institute Taloustutkimus on behalf of the Eurooppalainen Suomi association, daily Helsingin Sanomat said left-leaning MPs with trade union ties would decide the outcome.

"Mainly the members of parliament who support the conditions set by the trade union movement will come to play a decisive role," the paper said, adding that the current number of pro-EMU MPs was not big enough for a majority vote in favour of joining.
Among the terms for EMU entry demanded by trade unions and referred to by many MPs in the poll the most crucial one is that employment in Finland should improve decisively.
Unions also want so called buffer funds to dampen the impact on employment and wages of business cycle swings, and say that the Finnish collective bargaining system should remain intact.

Last December, daily Iltalehti conducted its own EMU poll among MPs and found 55 in favour of EMU, 44 against and 60 undecided. The rest it had not been able to reach or they had declined to give their opinion.
